llm.summary: This memory skill is mostly coherent, but it persistently records and reuses conversations and can sync verbatim archives to a NAS using stored credentials without strong scoping or retention controls.

dimensions.detail: Local memory files are expected, but remote NAS sync to fixed hosts and use of a local NAS credential env file add sensitive network-write and credential-handling exposure.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is simple symlinking of local scripts into PATH; metadata does not declare bounded permissions, so operators must infer file, shell, and network authority from the documentation and scripts.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions tell agents to read memory before answering, treat memory files as source of truth, log user and assistant content after every interaction, and use periodic session dumping, with limited user consent, redaction, retention, or deletion guidance.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates persistent daily logs, mesh data, decisions, checkpoints, quarter notes, PDF archives, and NAS copies, with no clear expiry and a vault-push script that explicitly never deletes.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated memory purpose matches logging, search, checkpointing, PDFs, and NAS sync, but the capability set captures every interaction, creates verbatim durable archives, restores context after wipes, and even advertises retaining secrets.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intentionally want an agent to persist conversation history across sessions and possibly replicate verbatim archives to a NAS. Configure redaction and retention first, avoid logging passwords or private keys, disable NAS sync unless needed, and prefer restricted SSH keys over password-based sshpass.
llm.findings:
[TT2] unexpected: The decision filename only lowercases and replaces spaces, so path separators in a topic could write outside the intended decisions directory; this is a real implementation bug, not core memory behavior.
[LP3] unexpected: The artifact directs file reads/writes, shell use, and network-adjacent workflows without a permissions manifest or tight path boundaries.
[TP4] expected: Archival, checkpointing, recovery, and NAS sync are disclosed as part of the memory system, so this is not hidden tool poisoning, but the high-impact data flows need clearer opt-in controls.
[SDI-2] expected: NAS credential loading and authenticated rsync are consistent with vault sync, but they materially expand blast radius and should be treated as sensitive optional setup.
[SQP-2] expected: Automatic logging and verbatim PDF archival are explicit features, but the main skill instructions do not provide strong privacy warnings or minimization before capture.
[SSD-3] expected: Long-term retention and resurfacing are central to this memory skill, but blanket retention, crash recovery from archives, and references to stored secrets make it a Review concern.
[PE3] expected: Using sshpass with NAS_PASS from a local env file is purpose-aligned for NAS sync but is a sensitive credential pattern that should be replaced or tightly constrained.
[RA2] expected: Session persistence is expected for a memory bridge, but it is broad, durable, and reused automatically across sessions without clear boundaries.
